name: vrnetlab (original)
what_it_is: vrnetlab packages commercial virtual router disk images into Docker containers that run full KVM-based emulation, enabling programmatic network testing and CI/CD workflows without distributing pre-built images. Originally developed for Deutsche Telekom's TeraStream project.
components: vr-xcon (inter-router TCP socket bridge for p2p interface linking)
Cisco Nexus NX-OS (Titanium) router image builder
measurement: No built-in telemetry or measurement framework documented
SNMP polling available on port 161 per router container
configuration: SSH access on port 22 per router container
NETCONF on port 830 per router container
Serial console via Telnet on port 5000 per router container
Inter-router interface links via vr-xcon TCP sockets on ports 10001-10099
Custom Docker images built locally from vendor-supplied disk images
No configuration persistence across container restarts (stateless by design)
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection framework documented
modes: CI/CD automated testing mode (primary design target)
constraints: Users must supply their own vendor-licensed disk images; no pre-built router images are distributed due to commercial license restrictions
Requires Linux host with KVM support and nested virtualization; incompatible with xhyve and standard VirtualBox
No configuration persistence: container state is lost on restart, intentional for stateless CI workflows
Resource consumption equivalent to running full virtual machines, not lightweight containers
Cannot integrate directly with standard Docker-networked containers without workarounds
docker_services: vr-xcon — inter-router connector container that bridges router interface TCP sockets for point-to-point links
Per-router containers (one per router instance, built locally from vendor disk image)
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml at repository root (topology files are user-defined per deployment)
No pre-built images on Docker Hub due to vendor license restrictions
No built-in topology orchestration (users script container startup and vr-xcon wiring manually)
No GUI or web interface for lab management
No native Windows or macOS support (KVM is Linux-only)
